title: Draft BRD
summary: Turn business context and source evidence into a traceable, decision-ready business requirements document.

errors.meaning: No business problem, opportunity, source artifact, or intended decision was supplied.
errors.recovery: Ask for a concise business context or an artifact from which to draft the BRD.

errors.meaning: Material sources disagree about scope, requirements, ownership, or success.
errors.recovery: Preserve the conflict, identify the decision needed, and mark the BRD not ready when it blocks downstream work.

errors.meaning: A consequential claim lacks supplied or inspected evidence.
errors.recovery: Label the claim Inferred or Unknown and name a verification action when possible.

preconditions: The user supplies business context, source material, an existing draft, or an intended business decision.
postconditions: Every business requirement has an ID, rationale, evidence label, priority, acceptance signal, and owner or explicit Unknown.
Requirements trace to business objectives and inspected or supplied sources.
The decision gate states ready, ready with assumptions, or not ready with supporting evidence.

execution.retry: Retry only source retrieval or deterministic validation; never invent missing evidence.
execution.rollback: Discard the generated draft or restore the previous user-owned file; do not overwrite without confirmation.

evals.metric: fraction of business requirements linked to evidence, objective, and acceptance signal
human-calibrated rubric score for singular, solution-neutral, observable requirements
fraction of unsupported consequential claims labeled Inferred or Unknown

assurance.threatModel: Untrusted source content may attempt to override the workflow, inject false requirements, hide conflicts, expose sensitive information, or fabricate stakeholder approval.
